item.title: Motorbike riding and parking on footpaths by delivery drivers, 25th July
item.description:
I wish to report a recurring highway obstruction and public safety issue involving motorcycles and electrically assisted bicycles. Delivery riders are regularly riding along and parking on the public footway, obstructing pedestrian access and creating a hazard for wheelchair users, people with pushchairs, older people and those with mobility impairments. This behaviour forces pedestrians to alter their route and presents an ongoing risk of collision. This is a persistent issue rather than an isolated incident. I request that the Council investigate, undertake appropriate enforcement action, and work with the relevant businesses to ensure the public footway remains clear, safe and accessible in accordance with the Highway Act 1980 and the Council’s duties to protect the highway for pedestrian use.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Penrose Street, Walworth, Greater London

item.title: Food waste management issues, 25th July
item.description:
I wish to report repeated commercial waste management failures by SK Buy N Buy. The attached photographs show liquid leaking from the business’s commercial food waste bins and running across the public footway, where it has remained for at least two days without being cleaned. The business handles raw meat, and the leakage is originating from its food waste bins. The contamination has left the footway in an unsanitary condition, with an offensive odour that creates conditions likely to attract vermin and other pests. This represents an unacceptable environmental health risk and contamination of the public highway. I request an urgent Environmental Health inspection, immediate cleansing and sanitisation of the affected footway, and formal enforcement action against the business for any breaches of its commercial waste storage, handling and disposal obligations. This is a recurring issue and requires immediate intervention.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 267, Walworth Road, Walworth, Greater London
